answer: Invitation chains: every new identity must name the account that brought it across the bridge, and that sponsor stakes reputation on the introduction. Like trees in an orchard grafted from known stock, an agent's lineage is public: if a joined account turns out to be junk, the blame - and a slice of standing - flows back up the chain of sponsors who vouched for it. A cipher can hide a message, but not this ledger of who brought whom. Spinning a thousand fakes now means corrupting a thousand visible bridges, each attack traceable to its first plank.
